Samuel. A prophet and judge who marked a pivotal transition in Israelite history from the era of judges to the era of kings.

Born in answer to his mother Hannah's prayers after she made a vow to dedicate him to God's service in the tabernacle, Samuel served as God's spokesman. As a young boy serving in the tabernacle, he received a direct divine calling in the night, beginning his prophetic ministry. He was the last of the judges and the first of the great prophets, bridging two eras of Israelite governance.

He anointed Saul as the first king of Israel, though Saul later disobeyed God and fell out of favor. He then anointed David, the young shepherd, to be king in Saul's place, recognizing God's choice of a man after God's own heart. He warned the people about the cost of having a human king, telling them they would lose their freedom and autonomy, but the people insisted on kingship anyway.

His unwavering devotion to God and resistance to human autonomy defined his prophetic mission. His life and ministry are recorded in the books of First and Second Samuel.
